title: The front-matter codec is line-oriented: collections must stay inline
body: parse_front_matter iterates block.split("\n") and matches one key per line, so any YAML block sequence or nested mapping breaks parsing outright. OKF typed links are written as inline flow mappings ([{target: "slug", rel: "relates-to"}]) for exactly this reason — valid YAML that an external reader parses and this codec can still own. Adding a structured field? Keep it on one line.

title: Don't hand-build page front matter in eval fixtures
body: eval/corpus.py, eval/realistic.py, and eval/selection.py each kept their own copy of the front-matter dict and all three silently went stale when the page format changed. Build a WikiNode and call wiki_store.node_front_matter(node) instead — one mapping, one place to update.

title: Adopting an external format means taking its semantics, not just its names
body: OKF v0.2 rewrites `timestamp` on every edit, so mapping Memex's immutable `created` onto it would have let any OKF tool destroy the creation date. Before renaming a field to match an external spec, read that spec's writer to see when it mutates the field — the name is the cheap half of conformance.

title: Hatchling ships in-package files; force-include entries for them are dead config
body: Two force-include entries existed for dashboard.css and htmx.min.js even though both sit inside the package. Building a wheel with those lines deleted produced an identical wheel. Before adding a packaging entry for an asset, build without it and check the wheel contents — and prefer putting runtime assets inside the package so no entry is needed at all.

title: Never resolve package paths by counting parents of __file__
body: packaged_marketplace() walked a fixed number of parents from __file__ to find its assets. Moving the module one directory deeper broke harness installation, caught only by two tests. Anchor on the package root by name — next(p for p in Path(__file__).parents if p.name == 'memex') — so the lookup survives any move.

title: Incremental update of a generated file: parse to the render's middle form, keep lines verbatim, serialize through one composer
body: To splice one row into a generated file while guaranteeing byte equality with a full render, split the renderer into (a) a structured middle form (here: entry lines per type per slug + child names) and (b) one composer that serializes it. The incremental path parses the existing file back into that middle form keeping every untouched line verbatim (only inspecting the link to identify and sort rows), edits one entry, and re-serializes through the same composer. Anything the parser does not recognise returns None and takes the full render path, so a wrong guess costs time, never bytes. A seeded randomized sequence asserting diagnose() == [] after every step is the cheap oracle.

title: Count file opens by spying on Path.read_text, not builtins.open
body: pathlib's Path.read_text/open call io.open directly, so monkeypatching builtins.open sees none of the store's or classifier's reads. Patch Path.read_text (filter by suffix and root) to count page and index opens; use monkeypatch.undo() between measurements so the spy list is per-operation. Also: never name a scratch script profile.py; it shadows the stdlib profile module and cProfile fails to import.

title: Benchmark tuples drift with any retriever change in the shared tree
body: All four strategies' rendered-token counts move whenever snippet or query-term logic in bm25_retriever.py changes, even for strategies unrelated to your slice. Record the tuples with a direct `run_benchmark()` print before touching anything (the test only shows the first mismatching tuple), and isolate your own effect with an off/on run in the same tree (e.g. bind `agent_workflow.build_injection = partial(build_injection, depth=0)`) rather than trusting before/after runs made while other agents edit the retriever.

title: The workflow fixture has no resolvable wiki links
body: Only 2 of 123 cards contain `[[...]]` and all four targets (`slug`, `ruff-linter`) are slugs no card has, so any link-graph mechanism scores exactly like the baseline on this benchmark. A linked-cards fixture is required before claiming coverage gains from expansion.

title: Reserve the trailing marker before packing a budgeted section
body: When a rendered section ends with an omitted-count marker, subtract the marker's `estimate_tokens` (sized for the maximum possible count) from the budget before adding entries, then stop at the first entry that does not fit. Sum-of-part estimates with `len//4+1` are always >= the estimate of the joined text, so the section stays within budget without a second rendering pass.

title: Per-row Path.resolve dominates a filesystem scan
body: Calling Path.resolve() (realpath) once per parsed row cost 45 of 69 ms per ten navigation searches on a 500-page store. Resolve the containing directory once per file and validate each leaf lexically (a single safe component, checked with the existing check_slug); the same containment guarantee at one-third the time.

title: Compute expectations before installing a forbidding spy
body: A test that monkeypatches Path.read_text to raise on page files must compute any expected values that read those files (e.g. the front-matter end offset) before the patch is installed; otherwise the assertion phase trips its own spy and reports a false failure in the code under test.

title: zsh does not word-split an unquoted variable
body: In this repository's zsh shell, `F="a.py b.py"; uv run ruff format $F` passes one argument containing spaces and fails with 'No such file or directory'. List the files explicitly or use ${=F} when a variable must expand to several arguments.
